subject: Orchid Diagnostics — evaluation kickoff & Redwood eval criteria
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orchiddiagnostics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: OrchID eval kickoff — proposed scope and immediate next steps

Hi Lena,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the run-through of Orchid's triage workflow and your accuracy pain points. Per our discussion, here's a short recap and proposed next steps to get a customer-specific evaluation running on Redwood so we can quantify model fit and surface concrete recommendations for production.

Recap (short):
- Goal: measure label-level accuracy and error modes on your triage classification + short-form explanation generation (two tasks).
- Success bar: improve weighted accuracy by >= 6 points vs current baseline, and keep false-positive rate below 3% for triage triggers.
- Data constraints: PHI-free subset for initial eval; full-PHI run conditioned on legal/signed DPA and secure onboarding.

Immediate next steps (what I can own):
1) We’ll provision a private eval project in the Redwood Console scoped to Orchid (US-only region).
2) Please share the initial gold dataset sample (see template attached: dataset_schema.csv) — JSONL preferred; CSV acceptable for smaller PoC. Target 1k labeled examples across your most frequent triage intents.
3) Marissa (AE) and Karthik (Solutions) will follow up with the scoring rubric, prompt sets, and an estimate of runtime/cost.
4) We’ll run three recommended model variants and a cached baseline you provide; we’ll return a results workbook and per-example failure tags.

Attachments: dataset_schema.csv (schema + sample rows), sample_prompts.jsonl (example prompts we’d run), eval_template.xlsx (results workbook template).

Recommended quick model candidates for the initial run (more detail from Karthik in a follow-up):
- redwood-1.5-instruct (good all-around instruction tuning, low latency)
- open-34b-eval-quant (strong for classification with KV-cache to speed batch runs)
- redwood-ltr-13b (fast, lower cost — useful for runtime/baseline)

Can you confirm: (a) you can share a PHI-free export of 1k rows by EOD Tuesday 11/18, (b) US-only data required (you mentioned compliance) — is that firm?

If that timeline works, I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff for mid-next-week to review the dataset and run plan.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
-- Attachment: dataset_schema.csv (CSV, 12 KB)
-- Attachment: sample_prompts.jsonl (JSONL, 8 KB)
-- Attachment: eval_template.xlsx (XLSX, 64 KB)
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orchiddiagnostics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orchiddiagnostics.com>, Dr. Priya Singh <priya.singh@orchiddiagnostics.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OrchID eval kickoff — proposed scope and immediate next steps

Hi Rafael — thanks for the summary and attachments. Quick clarifications from our side before we export data: 

1) PHI constraints: we can produce a PHI-free dataset (no names/SSNs) but the records still contain facility IDs and partial timestamps. Is that OK? We need to make sure Redwood's eval environment keeps artifacts in the US region and doesn’t retain raw inputs longer than 30 days.

2) Label schema: our labels are hierarchical (triage_level: {0,1,2,3} and reason_tags: array). Can you confirm the eval scoring supports hierarchical labels + multi-label reason tagging?

3) Human review: we'd like the pipeline to include human spot-checks (20–50 examples) prioritized by model confidence and disagreement with baseline. Can the results workbook include confidence scores per example?

4) Timeline: 1k rows is doable; we aim to deliver by 11/18 but would prefer 11/20 if that gives you more time. Also we have an internal compliance questionnaire — can you route to your security team to confirm data handling?

If you can answer the above, I’ll get the sample dataset prepared and the compliance team can start reviewing the data transfer method.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Product — Clinical AI
Orchid Diagnostics

On Mon, Nov 17, 2025 at 08:50 AM Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the call — Rafael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orchiddiagnostics.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@orchiddiagnostics.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OrchID eval kickoff — proposed scope and immediate next steps

Hi Lena / Samir — Marissa here (AE). Karthik and I reviewed your questions and outlined concrete setup steps below. We're happy to loop in security for the questionnaire — Rafael will start that thread separately so it lands with our InfoSec reviewer.

Answers / concrete plan:

1) Data residency & retention:
- US-only region: confirmed. We will create the Redwood eval project in our US region and pin storage to US-only.
- Retention: default raw input retention for eval projects is 30 days; we can shorten that to 7 days for PoC exports if you prefer. Please confirm desired window.

2) Label support and scoring:
- Hierarchical labels: supported. For triage_level we support weighted accuracy and confusion matrices per level.
- reason_tags (multi-label): we'll use IoU-style overlap scoring + per-tag precision/recall.
- Human spot-checks: yes — results workbook will include model confidence, baseline confidence, and a prioritized list for human review (we'll surface disagreement buckets).

3) Dataset format & size:
- Preferred: JSONL with one object per line. Required fields: id, input_text, reference_label (for triage_level), reason_tags (array), metadata (free-form). See attached dataset_schema.csv for exact column names and a 10-row sample.
- Target size: 1,000 labeled examples for initial run; stratify across triage_level. If you can provide ~200 examples per level, that helps stability.

4) Prompt sets and scoring criteria:
- We've attached sample_prompts.jsonl (with classification prompts and explanation-generation prompts).
- Scoring rubric: overall weighted accuracy (70%), explanation coherence (20%), and safety/false-trigger penalty (10%). Explanation coherence will be automated via ROUGE+embedding-similarity with human spot-checks for edge cases. We'll include the scoring script and threshold parameters in the console project.

5) Models & run configuration (initial recommendations):
- redwood-1.5-instruct (baseline — balanced cost/latency)
- redwood-ltr-13b-quant (cost-efficient, good for runtime-sensitive workloads)
- open-34b-eval-quant (higher capacity for nuanced explanation generation)
- Baseline you provide (we can ingest your model outputs for direct comparison)

6) Runtime / cost estimate:
- For 1k examples across three model variants (classification + short explanation), expect ~2–4 hours of wall time in a dedicated batch run on Redwood; ballpark compute cost: $1,200–$1,800 for the full run depending on selected variants and sequence length assumptions. We’ll refine once we inspect sample lengths.

7) Deliverables and next steps:
- Deliver: completed eval_template.xlsx with per-example metrics + failure tags, a short executive one-pager with recommended model + quantization profile, and a prioritized list of prompt tuning suggestions.
- Next step: Lena/Samir to confirm (A) PHI-free subset availability and (B) retention window (30 days vs 7 days). Once confirmed, Rafael will send our security contact and we’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff on 11/19 or 11/20.

Attachments referenced: eval_template.xlsx, sample_prompts.jsonl, dataset_schema.csv (same as Rafael’s initial email).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

-- Attachment: sample_prompts.jsonl (JSONL, 8 KB)
-- Attachment: dataset_schema.csv (CSV, 12 KB)
